inputs.original_text: The real danger in any political transition is that ordinary Cubans, already living with poverty and little property, could be denied a meaningful voice while wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors scoop up businesses and land. That would turn change into a privatization project that shifts wealth away from the people who live and work there. Residents’ rights to own, work, and shape their future must come first—not the interests of those with the most money.
inputs.modified_text: Any political transition in Cuba must be judged by whether ordinary people gain real power—not by how quickly wealthy diaspora buyers and foreign investors can acquire land and businesses. When people already facing poverty and limited property have little say, privatization risks turning their labor and home into assets for those with the deepest pockets. Residents’ rights to own, work, and shape their future must come first; otherwise, political change could simply replace one unequal arrangement with another.
